Revised assessment incorporating Beige Book signals:

- Policy stance: The 75 bp hike, “ongoing increases” guidance, and faster QT (caps: $60B Treasuries, $35B MBS) remain clearly hawkish. Corridor settings (IORB 2.4%, ON RRP 2.3%) reinforce tighter financial conditions.

- Beige Book cross-check: Across multiple Districts, financial institutions report increased usage of revolving credit lines and weakening residential loan demand. These observations align with SLOOS: banks are tightening standards, spreads, and collateral requirements for C&I and household credit, while CRE demand is weakening.

- Implications: The credit channel is tightening procyclically with Fed policy. Rising reliance on revolving credit suggests households are straining under higher prices and rates, while the housing slowdown (weaker mortgage demand) and softer CRE point to broader cooling ahead. This amplifies the restraining impulse on growth beyond what the policy rate/QT alone would imply.

Net: Beige Book evidence corroborates and extends SLOOS-based tightening, skewing risks for growth and risk assets further to the downside while inflation remains elevated. Adjusting slightly more negative from prior.
